title: Atomic charge & latency mapper for per-route/model/customer breakdown
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: The Console currently shows coarse cost/latency numbers per account and model but cannot consistently answer fine-grained questions like: 'Which route consumed the most GPU-seconds last week?', 'How much of a tenant's token cost is due to KV cache misses?', or 'Which model variant caused the 99th percentile latency spike for route /chat/stream?'. Existing rollups conflate batching, prefix cache hits, and aborts, making per-route and per-model unit economics opaque.

Goal: Build an atomic decomposition and mapping service that consumes telemetry (request traces, kernel-level GPU time samples, batching metadata, cache hit markers) and produces shardable, queryable per-route/model/customer breakdowns of cost (GPU-time, IO, token units) and latency (p50/p95/p99, queuing vs execution). The service must be deterministic for a given input stream, support late-arriving metrics, and provide graceful degradation when partial telemetry is available.
spec:
High-level design:
- Input: normalized telemetry events from ingestion pipeline (trace-start, trace-end, batch-boundary, kv-cache-hit/miss, kernel-sample).
- Core idea: Emit atomic 'charge events' at the smallest accountable unit (atomic_unit) defined as a single inference token execution slice within a batch instance. Each atomic_unit carries provenance: route_id, model_id, tenant_id, batch_id, seq_index, cache_flag, kernel_tags.
- Attribution: Use deterministic apportioning rules to split batch-level GPU-time across constituent atomic_units using sequence length weights and measured kernel-samples. KV cache misses get an explicit multiplier. For requests with partial telemetry, use a probabilistic fallback trained from historical traces for sensible apportionment.
- Storage: Append-only Delta tables partitioned by date and tenant for backfill friendliness. Collate daily aggregates for Console queries.
- Query surface: Precompute per-route/model/customer aggregates (tokens, GPU-ms, IO, p50/p95/p99 latencies separated into queue vs exec) and expose via console-analytics read API.
- Backwards compatibility: Provide a compatibility layer that can accept legacy rollup records and reconcile them into atomic events with flagged uncertainty scores.
acceptance_criteria: 1) For synthetic workload with deterministic seeds, total GPU-ms computed by the mapper must reconcile within 0.5% of runtime-side GPU telemetry for the same time window.
2) Per-route and per-model aggregates are available in Console queries within 10 minutes of ingestion for >95% of events in steady-state.
3) For requests annotated with cache-hit flags, computed per-token cost delta vs baseline is consistent with benchmarking harness within +/- 10%.
4) The service exposes an uncertainty score for each aggregate to indicate reliance on probabilistic fallbacks.
5) Automated integration tests cover failure modes: missing kernel-samples, late-arriving batch-end events, and partial tenant telemetry.
tasks: Design protobuf schema for atomic_unit and charge_event (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console-telemetry/pull/248)
Build mapper prototype as a Flink job that consumes daily telemetry topic and emits atomic events to delta lake partition (branch: feat/atomic-mapper)
Integrate deterministic apportioner library from runtime team and add kernel-sample weighting logic
Implement probabilistic fallback model: lightweight gradient-boosted regressor trained on last 30 days of complete traces
Create reconciliation job to ingest legacy rollups and emit uncertainty-annotated atomic events
Add daily aggregate materialized view and API endpoint for Console UI
End-to-end test against runtime load generator (conftest harness) and create alerting for mapper lag > 15m
updates: 2026-02-10 - Ticket created by Ava Patel. Initial scoping and impact assessment completed. Identified runtime-provided kernel-samples and batch metadata as critical inputs.
2026-02-18 - Protobuf schema v0.1 drafted; shared in #console-backend. Feedback from Infra: include batch_id sequence and per-gpu-index timing. Action: update schema.

2026-02-27 - Prototype Flink job ingesting telemetry topic works end-to-end for synthetic load. Observed 6% overcount in GPU-ms vs runtime profiler due to duplicated kernel-samples; root cause traced to sampler dedup logic. Fix implemented and merged (PR 256).

2026-03-03 - Met with PM (Riley Chen) and Design (Maya Singh) to align on Console surface. Decided to show uncertainty score and allow Console to toggle probabilistic adjustments. PM requested exportable CSV for finance reconciliation.

2026-03-08 - Ran a 24h A/B validation: old rollups vs atomic mapper. Atomic mapper revealed previously unobserved skew in route /embed/bulk where cache misses inflated GPU-time. Raised ENG-157812 to patch runtime cache marker emission.
2026-03-14 - Current: Mapper running in dev cluster with 10% of prod traffic. Latency for aggregates ~6m. Next: increase to 50% canary and run financial reconciliation job.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Late-arriving events will cause aggregates to change and confuse Console users. Mitigation: emit uncertainty_score and show last_updated timestamp; also retain a 7-day backfill window with visible change-logs.
Risk: Over-attribution when kernel-samples are sparse. Mitigation: fallback model with conservative apportioning and flagging of high-uncertainty tenants.
Risk: Performance impact of Flink job during peak. Mitigation: autoscaling, checkpoint tuning, and offloading heavy ML fallback to offline batch if bridge compute is high.
Risk: Reconciliation mismatches with billing. Mitigation: run reconciliation pipeline with finance team and create acceptance tolerances; exportable proof-of-truth CSV for audits.
review_feedback: PM Riley Chen: 'Love the uncertainty score idea — make sure it's easy to explain to finance.'
Runtime lead Nikhil Rao: 'We can add per-request kernel-sample anchors from runtime which should reduce probabilistic fallback volume by ~60%.'
Security reviewer Lina Gomez: 'No secrets in telemetry, but ensure PII scrubber runs pre-ingest.'
acceptance_test_plan: Deploy to staging with synthetic trace generator that covers edge cases (partial telemetry, heavy batching, high cache miss patterns).
Run reconciliation job comparing sum(mapper.GPU_ms) vs runtime_profiler.GPU_ms across tenants for a 24h window; pass threshold <0.5%
Run load test at 2x peak ingestion rate for 1h and assert mapper lag < 15 minutes and <5% event drop
Validate Console UI imports CSV and that exported totals match materialized views
